transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is I feel like I’m always up and moving. Even on a quiet day, I’ll be bouncing from the garden club list to my knitting bag to some travel papers, and I haven’t really finished any one thing before I’m on to the next. It’s not terrible, but it’s been noticeable.
Did this tendency to jump from one task to another start when you were a child?

Yes, I think so. Even back in grade school, my teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but scattered. I was always losing papers, talking when I shouldn’t, and wiggling around in my seat before I’d even finished my work.
Do these problems with staying focused and finishing things interfere with your work or daily responsibilities?

Yes, it does. I’m not working now, but at home and at the community center it’s started to cause strain. My husband, and the other volunteers too, can’t really count on me to keep plans straight unless someone checks behind me. It’s embarrassing, honestly.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy compared with your normal self?
I don’t think so. I have days where I’m busy or kind of wound up, but I wouldn’t say I’ve felt unusually high or euphoric, not like that.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks and activities?

Yes, I do. I end up with piles of things all over the kitchen table—stuff for dance class, knitting, garden events, trips—and then I look at it all and I can’t always tell what needs to be done first. It gets kind of jumbled.
Are you often easily distracted by things going on around you?
Yes, pretty often. If someone’s talking in the next room, or even a car goes by the window, my mind just jumps over to that and I lose track of what I was doing.
Do you tend to spend so much time trying to make things exactly right that it delays getting them finished?
I don’t think that’s really a big problem for me. I might fuss with something a little, but I don’t usually get stuck trying to make it perfect.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?
I’m not sure I’d say I worry a lot for no clear reason. I mean, I have normal worries like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed it being a big constant thing.
